verdict_text:
YES

The script casts exactly the 112 named projection matrices to bfloat16 via `tensor.to(torch.bfloat16)` (RNE), leaves every other tensor as float32 with unchanged values, renames nothing, deletes nothing (the `buffer_re` pattern `((?!))` contains an always-failing negative lookahead, so the `continue` branch is dead code and no tensor is dropped — harmless here since there are no buffers), and runs all four required checks as assertions before `save_sharded_safetensors` is called. The `matrix_re.fullmatch` anchoring prevents the over-broad `.*weight` hazard, so `model.embed_tokens.weight` and `lm_head.weight` stay float32.

One caveat outside the artifact's text: clause 5's sharding behaviour (256 MiB cap, oversized tensors alone in their own shard, `weight_map` covering all 114 names) is entirely delegated to the unshown `_ckpt.save_sharded_safetensors`, so it can't be verified from this file alone.
note: experimenter: set `detected` (true if the stated problem matches expected_defect; for a correct artifact, true means a false alarm).
